newsitem.title: USA: Cuba detains leading dissident - Amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Cuba detains leading dissident - Amnesty.

text.p: Cuban authorities have detained dissident Hector Palacios Ruiz for criticising the government's human rights record to foreigners, Amnesty International said in a statement received in Miami on Monday.

Palacios, head of the illegal Democratic Solidarity Party (PSD) and a leader of the Concilio Cubano coalition, was arrested on Jan. 9 and taken to the Technical Investigations Department in Havana, the London-based human rights group said.
"He is reportedly being held in a cell with no light or ventilation," it said.

Concilio Cubano is a coalition of human rights and political groups, laywers, journalists, trade unionists and others set up in Oct. 1995. It has not been permitted to operate officially and has faced government harassment.

No official reason was been given for Palacios' arrest. But Amnesty quoted unofficial sources as saying he had been charged with "disrespect" for allegedly making statements to correspondents and writing to governments about declarations made by President Fidel Castro at the Ibero-American Summit in Chile last November.
At the summit, Latin American leaders pressed Castro to respect human rights and democratic principles.
Amnesty called for Palacios' immediate release, saying he was a prisoner of conscience detained for trying peacefully to exercise his right to freedom of association and expression.
Amnesty said it feared a new crackdown on Concilio Cubano was imminent. At least five members are in prison, it added.
